rawFindings.title: Incorrect usage of RegExp in string replacement
rawFindings.explanation: The original code uses a RegExp with the global flag to replace all '%' characters: new RegExp('%', 'g'). The change replaces it with a string '%' which only replaces the first occurrence, which changes the behavior and likely breaks scripts that have multiple '%' placeholders.
rawFindings.suggestion: Revert to using a global RegExp for replacing all '%' characters: var placeholder = new RegExp('%', 'g'); var cmdString = mout.string.replace(config.scripts[action], placeholder, orderedPackages.join(' '));

rawFindings.title: Incorrect replacement of all '%' placeholders in scripts
rawFindings.explanation: The original code used a regular expression with the global flag (/g) to replace all occurrences of the '%' character in the script command string. The modified code uses a simple string '%' without a global regex, resulting in only the first '%' being replaced. This changes the behavior, potentially leaving un-replaced placeholders causing incorrect command invocation.
rawFindings.suggestion: Restore the use of RegExp with global flag for replacing all '%' placeholders with ordered package names: use RegExp('%', 'g') instead of simple string '%'. Alternatively, ensure to replace all occurrences to preserve original behavior.

rawFindings.title: Incorrect replacement of all '%' placeholders with only the first occurrence
rawFindings.explanation: The original code replaced all '%' characters in the script string using a global regular expression, ensuring every placeholder was replaced with the joined package names. The new code replaces only the first occurrence because the string '%' was used without a global flag, which changes the behavior and likely breaks scripts expecting multiple substitutions.
rawFindings.suggestion: Restore the global replacement by using a global regular expression: var placeholder = new RegExp('%', 'g'); and use it in the replace method as before.
